data.long_meaning: Calestian is a Latin name derived from 'Calestes' or 'Calistus'. In Christian history, Calistus was a Pope and a saint, and the name is often given to those dedicated to him. The name Calestian carries the meaning “Dedicated to Calistus” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Calestian usually hope their child will grow to embody dedicated to calistus and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Calestian Order of Monks, also known as the Calistians, was a monastic order founded in the late 12th century in Italy.
historical_references.context: The order was founded by Calixtus II (1119-1198), Pope from 1119 to 1130 and 1133 to 1143. He named the order after himself, and it was known for its strict adherence to the Rule of St. Benedict and its focus on caring for the sick and the poor.

historical_references.reference: Calestian, also known as Calistus, was a 4th-century martyr who was a deacon in Rome and was put to death during the Diocletian Persecution.
historical_references.context: Calestian is said to have been tortured and then beheaded for refusing to renounce his faith. He is venerated as a saint in the Catholic and Orthodox Churches and is remembered for his steadfastness in the face of persecution.
